Lecture one: MIS
A system is a combination or arrangement of parts to form an integrated whole according to some common principles or rules. A system is a group of interrelated components working together toward a common goal by accepting inputs and producing outputs in an organized transformation process. three basic interacting components or functions:
●	Input: involves capturing and assembling elements that enter the system to be processed. For example, raw materials, energy, data, and human efforts must be secured and organized for processing.
●	Processing: involves transformation process that converts input into output. Examples are a manufacturing process, or mathematical calculations.
●	Output: involves transferring elements that have been produced by a transformation process to their ultimate destination. For example, finished products, human services, and management information must be transmitted to their human users.
Feedback is data about the performance of a system. For example, data about sales performance is feedback to a sales manager. 
 
The Basic Structure of Any Information System 
Question 1 (Understanding)
👉 System: Hospital Laboratory (Laboratory Testing System)
●	Input: Patient samples (such as blood or urine) alongside a laboratory request form.
●	Process: Laboratory equipment and technicians analyse the samples and process the test results.
●	Output: A formal laboratory report, such as blood test findings or diagnostic results.
●	Feedback: Clinical or system responses such as “abnormal result detected,” “repeat test required,” or “report ready for review.
“Lab system takes samples, analyzes them, produces reports, and improves accuracy through feedback.
Task (Individual or Pair Work – activity
Your Task: System Deconstruction
Reconstruct your chosen system by clearly identifying and logically linking the following elements:
●	🟢 Input: What initiates the system? (data, requests, materials, or participants)
●	🔵 Process: What transformations occur within the system? (analysis, validation, decision-making steps)
●	🟣 Output: What is produced or delivered as a result? (reports, services, decisions)
●	🟠 Feedback: What information is returned to regulate or improve system performance?
One point where errors may occur in the system, and how an intelligent system could reduce them.
Note: Avoid description only — focus on function and relationship between components and Present your answer as a structured system model,

●	Perform high-speed high-volume, numerical computations (DSS)
●	Provide fast, accurate, reliable, and inexpensive communication within and between organizations, anytime, anyplace.
●	Store huge amounts of information in an easy to access, yet small space (database management)
●	Allow quick and inexpensive access to vast amounts of information worldwide at any time
●	Enable collaboration any where anytime
●	Increase the effectiveness and efficiency of people working in groups in one place or in several 
locations (ex. data exchange, video conferencing)
●	Facilitate global trade (ex. thaigem.com)
●	Enable automation of routing decision making(ROP)
●	Can be wireless, thus supporting unique applications
